title: Housing funding rules, landfill work and transit changes
subtitle: Landfill expropriation, paramedic dispatch advocacy, grants, water licences, Ayr waste collection and a surplus Elmira property
overview: Regional Council approved a new approach to community housing as provider mortgages mature. Staff will draft a funding model and an annual reinvestment plan, and a new asset limit policy was endorsed for rent-geared-to-income households {{vote:m8}}. Council also asked the province to adopt a Medical Priority Dispatch System at the Cambridge ambulance communications centre.

Council approved the expropriation of a property on Snyder's Road in Wilmot for soil management at the Waterloo landfill, and passed the related by-law. It accepted a tender for a new landfill cell liner and leachate collection system, and a five-year contract for hazardous waste transportation and processing.

Other approvals include 2023 grant envelopes {{vote:m9}}, transit service improvements from September 4, 2023, the University Avenue design concept with reserved bike lanes, endorsement of 11 drinking water licences, and extended waste collection in downtown Ayr. A property at 22 Mockingbird Drive in Elmira was declared surplus and will go to the Township of Woolwich {{vote:m11}}. Public Health also gave a COVID update.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to build a funding model and annual reinvestment plan for community housing as mortgages end, endorsed a new asset limit policy, and asked the province to adopt a Medical Priority Dispatch System in Cambridge {{vote:m8}}.

Council approved a package including transit improvements from September 4, 2023, the University Avenue design with reserved bike lanes, 11 drinking water licences, the Heidelberg water supply report and Ayr waste collection expansion.
Council enacted By-law 23-013 to expropriate 2322 Snyder's Road East in Wilmot for soil management at the Waterloo landfill.
Council accepted Arcadis Canada Inc.'s tender of $8,695,067.73 plus taxes for the Cell SE-5A/B liner and leachate system, and advanced $1,930,000 of financing from 2024 to 2023.
Council accepted GFL Environmental Services Inc.'s tender for a five-year term from April 1, 2023, estimated at $2,456,918.80 plus taxes, with two optional one-year renewals.
Council approved 2023 grant program envelopes totalling $5,603,820 {{vote:m9}}.
Council declared the property surplus and authorized its transfer to the Township of Woolwich for $2 {{vote:m11}}.
